core_obligations: Write the affine scheme as X = Spec(B) (proof line 7194).
Identify morphisms Spf(A) -> Spec(B) with continuous S-algebra maps B -> A with B discrete, using the formal-spectrum lemma (proof lines 7194-7197).
Observe that continuity is automatic for the discrete topology, so these are simply S-algebra maps (proof lines 7197-7198).
Identify those with morphisms Spec(A) -> Spec(B), which gives the bijection (proof lines 7198-7199).

difficulty_reason: For a weakly admissible topological S-algebra A and an affine scheme X over S, the lemma states that the natural map Mor_S(Spec(A), X) -> Mor_S(Spf(A), X) is bijective (statement lines 7180-7191). The proof writes X = Spec(B) and identifies, via the chapter's lemma describing morphisms of formal spectra, the morphisms Spf(A) -> Spec(B) with continuous S-algebra maps B -> A where B carries the discrete topology; those are exactly the S-algebra maps, which correspond to morphisms Spec(A) -> Spec(B) (proof lines 7193-7199). The level is H2: the whole content is the translation of one universal property into another, carried out explicitly for both directions.
